problems.description: Consecutive edges of a wire do not meet in 3D: edge N's end point and edge N+1's start point are separated by more than tolerance, so the wire is broken even though the edges are listed in traversal order. ShapeFix_Wireframe::FixWireGaps walks every wire of the whole shape (wires inside faces AND free wires not belonging to any face) and closes each 3D gap.

problems.description: Consecutive edges of a wire meet in 3D but their pcurves do not meet in the surface's UV space: evaluated at the shared vertex, the two pcurves land at different (u,v) positions beyond tolerance. The wire is parametrically broken even though 3D topology is fine. FixWireGaps closes these 2D gaps across all face-bound wires of the shape.

problems.description: A wire contains edges whose 3D length is below the working tolerance (sliver/tiny/zero-length edges — remnants of over-trimming, translated tangencies, or spurious boolean intersections). ShapeFix_Wireframe finds them shape-wide (CheckSmallEdges) and removes them by merging each small edge into an adjacent edge via curve concatenation (JoinEdges), honoring cross-face adjacency, seam status and a turn-angle limit; in drop mode a non-mergeable small edge is deleted outright; a tiny self-loop (start vertex == end vertex) is removed.

problems.description: A single face spans the full period of a closed surface (cylinder, cone, torus, sphere, periodic B-spline) and its wire contains a seam edge — one edge reused with two pcurves. Many receivers cannot ingest self-closed faces; ShapeUpgrade_ClosedFaceDivide detects the seam, computes the parametric gap between the seam's two pcurves, and splits the face into two or more non-closed patches (recursively, so a torus gets split in both U and V).

problems.description: A face's surface is geometrically closed (start and end of the parametric range meet in 3D within tolerance) but the wire carries NO edge marked as a seam — e.g. a cylinder whose seam was emitted as two ordinary coincident edges, or a trimmed patch covering all but a hair of the full period. ShapeUpgrade_ClosedFaceDivide falls back to a geometric closure test (IsUClosed/IsVClosed, plus a half-surface re-test for thin nearly-full-period faces) and splits the face even without seam markup.

problems.description: The geometry under a single face has smoothness below the required continuity level: typically a B-spline surface with an interior knot whose multiplicity equals the degree (a C0 crease line across the whole face), or a swept/offset/trimmed surface whose basis geometry is discontinuous. ShapeUpgrade_SplitSurfaceContinuity first tries to REMOVE the offending knot within tolerance (repairing knots that are formally C0 but geometrically smooth), and where removal fails it records the knot parameter as a split value so the face is divided into C1+ pieces.

problems.description: Adjacent faces of a shell lie on the same geometric surface (coplanar planes, co-axial same-radius cylinders/cones, identical B-spline surfaces) and are separated only by artificial edges that bound no real geometry change — the typical output of boolean fuses and fragmenting translators. ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain (UnifyFaces/IntUnifyFaces) verifies same-domain geometry within linear/angular tolerance and merges the faces into one, rebuilding outer/hole wires, preserving requested internal edges, and reconstructing a seam when the union wraps a periodic surface.

problems.description: A chain of edges joined at degree-2 vertices lies on the same geometric curve — collinear line segments, arcs of one circle (possibly closing into a full circle), or a spliceable B-spline/Bezier sequence — so the interior vertices are topologically unnecessary fragmentation. ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain (UnifyEdges -> MergeEdges/generateSubSeq -> MergeSeq/MergeSubSeq) validates co-curve geometry (parallel line directions, coincident circle centers within tolerance) and fuses each chain into a single edge, concatenating the pcurves on all adjacent faces (UnionPCurves).

problems.description: A closed body is encoded on a B-spline surface that is geometrically closed but NOT declared periodic (e.g. CATIA 'like-seam' cylinders): two faces share an edge carrying two pcurves on the same surface — behaving like a seam — yet the surface has no period, so ordinary unification cannot wrap around. During face unification OCCT detects the smooth seam-like edge, converts/declares the surface periodic (SetUPeriodic/SetVPeriodic, approximating to B-spline if needed), migrates all pcurves to the new periodic surface, and merges the faces across it.

problems.description: An elementary surface (plane, cylinder, cone, sphere, torus) is defined on a left-handed ('indirect') axis system — its coordinate frame determinant, combined with any mirroring in the face location, is negative — or a conical surface carries a negative semi-angle. Such surfaces violate OCCT's right-handed/direct conventions and flip normal/orientation semantics downstream. ShapeCustom_DirectModification (ShapeCustom::DirectFaces) detects the condition and redresses the surface by U- and/or V-reversing a copy, correcting pcurves and wire/face orientation accordingly.

line_verification_notes: SOURCE VERSION DRIFT: V3 was generated from a newer OCCT than V7_8_1 (it cites ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain.cxx:4477 in a file that has 4118 lines at bd2a789f, and ShapeFix_Wireframe FixSmallEdges at 507 vs actual 401). Every evidence line in the kept problems was re-located and verified directly in the pinned checkout: FixWireGaps 107/178/183/204; CheckSmallEdges 469/525; MergeSmallEdges 590/816/887/927/1028/1038/1053; ClosedFaceDivide::SplitSurface 70/102-103/162-163/173-174/194-195/238; SplitSurfaceContinuity::Compute 94/99-142/147-198/234-256/275-296; UnifySameDomain: UnionPCurves 1643, MergeSubSeq 2014 (degenerate 2031-2074, lines 2099/2119, circles 2109/2151/2206, bsplines 2262), generateSubSeq 2443, MergeEdges 2495, MergeSeq 2601, UnifyFaces 2767, IntUnifyFaces 2898 (angle 3015, IsSameDomain 3021, internal edges 3133/3152, periodicity 3221-3269, ReconstructMissedSeam calls 3494/3586/3618), UnifyEdges 3802. V3 MISSED: the V-direction knot handling in SplitSurfaceContinuity (RemoveVKnot at 281, split insert at 296 — V3 only listed the U branch); the second duplicated loose-wire block in MergeSmallEdges (lines ~1150-1540 mirror the face block for free wires); and the whole ShapeCustom_DirectModification repair (added as problem 11). ShapeUpgrade_SplitSurface section in V3 is entirely unlabeled '?' placeholders; I inspected the file and it is pure splitting machinery (segment/trim bookkeeping, split-value snapping to bounds within tolerance in SetU/VSplitValues) with no independent defect semantics — excluded wholesale. PACKAGE SURVEY — ShapeExtend: data structures and infrastructure only (WireData wire container, ComplexCurve/CompositeSurface aggregate geometry used by splitters, Status bit encoding, message registrators, Explorer); no repair logic; no new problems. ShapeConstruct: services, not healers — ProjectCurveOnSurface builds/rebuilds pcurves and is the engine behind ShapeFix_Edge::FixAddPCurve (missing-pcurve problem owned by the ShapeFix_Edge group); ShapeConstruct_Curve adjusts curve endpoints (service to gap fixing); JoinPCurves/JoinCurves serve edge merging (problems 3/8); MakeTriangulation is construction. No new problems. ShapeCustom: predominantly conversion-for-downstream-constraints (BSplineRestriction degree/continuity restriction, ConvertToBSpline/ConvertToRevolution/SweptToElementary, TrsfModification scaling, Curve2d simplification) — transformations of valid input, not defect repair — EXCEPT ShapeCustom_DirectModification, which genuinely repairs indirect (left-handed) elementary surfaces and negative-semi-angle cones; added as problem tkshh-indirect-elementary-surface-axes (GAP). ShapeProcessAPI: one class (ApplySequence), a convenience wrapper running configured ShapeProcess operator sequences; no repair logic of its own. FIXTURE SKEPTICISM: Twi068 .stp bytes verified (three >tolerance junction gaps 0.05/0.07/0.06); Tfa016 verified multi-face; Twi089 verified two-edge collinear wire; N154/Twi031/Gp013/Gs070/Gs085 existence and record semantics verified against catalog records. Merge-eligibility guard branches (angle limits, face-set equality, seam consistency, parallelism/center gates) were deliberately folded into their parent problems as repair-correctness criteria rather than counted as separate problems or excluded as noise.
